newsitem.title: UK: ACPC seeks USDA explanation over Brazil forecasts.
newsitem.headline: ACPC seeks USDA explanation over Brazil forecasts.

text.p: The Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) on Wednesday sought an explanation from the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) over its conflicting Brazil's coffee crop forecasts.
It said there were anomalies between the USDA's general coffee report released last month and its agricultural attache report released to the public on Tuesday.

A field report by a U.S. agricultural attache in Sao Paulo dated May 12 was made public on Tuesday in which the attache saw the 1997/98 harvest at 24 million bags versus 27.5 million bags the previous year.
On June 13, a USDA estimate put it at 28 million bags.

"In the spirit of promoting openness and transparency in published analysis, the ACPC would encourage the USDA to explain such a significant difference between the two reports, and whether the report released in June was prepared by its USDA agricultural attache, or perhaps an external sub-contracted party," the London-based ACPC said in a statement.

The ACPC said whilst a number of the reasons for strong production this year had been carried into the attache report, several important contrary factors had also been mentioned, particularly to those relating to issues of tree stress last winter.
The other factor was the irregularity of rainfall patterns that had led to unusual multiple flowerings this year and some consequent losses.

"This expectation of a drop in production brings the (attache) report in line with most other parties within the coffee industry -- including the Brazilian government, and many large international trade houses even if expectations of actual production size continue to differ."
